RagShortTexts: In 1264 at Lewes, Simon de Montfort routed royalists, capturing Henry III and Prince Edward.

Variants.Content: Lewes, fought on May 14, 1264, marked the high point of Simon de Montfort's rebellion. Montfort's reformist barons defeated the royalist army of Henry III, and the king and his brother Richard, King of the Romans, were taken prisoner. Prince Edward had pursued a force of London militia too far from the main royal line, and that over-extension left the flanks exposed. The rebels' reserve then took advantage of the gap. The battle gave Montfort control of the king's government, and he used his position to press for a more representative parliament.

The Mise of Lewes gave Montfort the power to govern England in the king's name, and it led to the summons of the 1265 parliament, where representatives of the commons sat alongside the lords. Burgesses and knights of the shire had to ride to Westminster at their own expense, and each town's clerk entered the names of its representatives in the record.
